history.content: WebSurfer, please provide a brief industry perspective: in inventory contexts, does "oldest" typically refer to the earliest release year or the earliest inventory-added date? We have both fields present.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: In rental inventory and cataloging contexts, "oldest" generally refers to the earliest release year of the title unless explicitly tied to a stock or acquisition timeline. If the question is a data lookup without specifying acquisition time, the common interpretation is earliest ReleaseYear among the items in the category.

mistake_reason: At step 22, the Assistant disregarded the FileSurfer’s verified result (that the oldest Blu-Ray by ReleaseYear is "Time-Parking 2: Parallel Universe") and the WebSurfer’s semantic guidance, as well as the Orchestrator’s explicit instruction to return that title. Instead, the Assistant prioritized its own interpretation (earliest InventoryAdded) without justification aligned to the task wording, producing a different title. This is a clear instance of inter-agent misalignment: Ignored Other Agent's Input (FM-2.5).
